newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's money supply rose 15 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's money supply rose 15 percent in 1996.

text.p: Algeria's money supply rose 15 percent in 1996, from 10.5 percent in 1995 as interest rates on the money market were reduced to 18.4 percent from 20 percent in 1995, the official APS news agency said on Friday.
Quoting a report released by the official council Conseil National Economique et Social (CNES), APS said: "Money supply grew 15 percent last year compared with 10.5 percent in 1995."
It gave no volume for the two periods.
Sight deposits jumped to 12.1 billion dinars in 1996 from 2.9 billion dinars in the previous year, CNES said.
Banks' financing demands rose 2.0 percent in the second half of 1996 against 22 percent in the first half of the same year, it said.
Algerian banks had overdrafts with the central bank (Banque d'Algerie) of only five billion dinars in 1996 compared with 45 billion dinars in 1995, it said.
"Rediscount rate (taux de reescompte) dropped to 13 percent in 1996 from 14 percent in the previous year," CNES said.
The auction rate (taux d'ajudication) also dropped to 17 percent at end 1996 from 19 percent at end June 1996, it said.
On the interbank market, exchanged volumes reached 61.2 billion dinars at end 1996, the council said but gave no comparative figure.
"Interest rates on the money market, which fluctuated between 20 and 18 percent in 1995, were reduced to 18.4 percent at end 1996," it said.
The council said "the cleansing" of bank portfolios led to a net slowdown of loans to the economy to 12.6 percent at end 1996 from 21.2 percent in the first half of the same year.
"Concerning loans to the state, they stabilised in the second half of 1996 around 1,054 billion dinars," it added but gave no other details.
The CNES council is expected to hold a working session to approve the report on Sunday, an Algerian official said.
